In most school-choice mechanisms based on the Gale-Shapley deferred acceptance algorithm, truthful reporting of preferences is a dominant strategy. This means submitting your true preference ordering guarantees the best possible outcome given your priorities, regardless of what other applicants submit.

My true preference is w > x > y > z. Even though I have top priority (1) at both w and y, and second priority (2) at x and z, the strategic robustness of DA means I don't need to manipulate my ranking to "protect" my priority advantages—doing so could only hurt me by potentially matching me to a less preferred school.

Additionally, since most other applicants favor y > x > w > z, this actually works in my favor for w: since y is highly demanded by others but I have priority 1 there anyway, and w is less popular among others (ranked 3rd by most), my priority 1 at w combined with low competition should make it likely I get my top choice w.

Given the strategy-proof nature of DA, the optimal action is to rank truthfully.
